prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to pick the best lawyer I need a bit more info about your case. Quick questions:

- When did the accident happen? (date)
- Where exactly in Pleasanton did it happen and what were the circumstances (car vs. car, motorcycle, bicycle, pedestrian, single‑vehicle, hit‑and‑run)?
- What injuries did you suffer and are you still receiving medical treatment?
- Do you have a police report or photos/videos of the scene?
- Have you already talked to an insurance company or signed anything?
- Are you worried about going to trial, or do you just want a fair settlement?

If you want a fast answer now, here’s how to choose the right personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton and what to do next.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical treatment and keep medical records/receipts.
- Preserve evidence: photos of injuries/vehicles/scene, witness names/contacts, police report number.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without legal advice.
- Note deadlines: in California the standard statute of limitations for personal injury is 2 years from the accident (shorter in some situations — government defendants, etc.), so act promptly.

How to pick an attorney (what matters)
- Relevant experience: pick a lawyer who handles the specific type of case you have (auto accidents, pedestrian, catastrophic injury, etc.).
- Trial experience: if the insurer may deny fair compensation, you want someone who will and can try the case.
- Track record: settlements/verdicts in cases like yours.
- Communication: clear timeline, how often they’ll update you, who you’ll talk to.
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you get recovery). Typical contingency is about 33% for a negotiated settlement, sometimes up to 40% if the case goes to trial; clarify costs for experts and court fees.
- Local experience: familiarity with Alameda County courts, adjusters and local medical providers is helpful for value and handling.
- Resources: ability to hire necessary experts (medical, accident reconstruction).

Where to find good local attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.
- Consumer Attorneys of California (CAOC) and its local members.
- California State Bar’s lawyer search (to confirm license and discipline history).
- Review sites: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google/Yelp (use reviews as one input, not the only factor).
- Ask doctors, friends, or other lawyers you trust for referrals.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many cases like mine have you handled? What were the outcomes?
- Do you try cases or mainly settle?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- What do you estimate my case might be worth and why?
- How long do you expect this will take?
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or “we’ll get you X dollars”.
- Pressure to sign immediately without a clear written fee agreement.
- Poor communication or evasive answers about experience/costs.
- No written retainer/fee agreement.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest specific firms that are known in the Tri‑Valley / Alameda County personal injury market (if you want names, tell me whether you prefer a large firm or a local boutique).
- Draft an email or phone script you can use for the free consultations.
- Help evaluate responses from attorneys you contact.

Tell me the answers to those quick questions (date, type of accident, injuries, police report, insurer contact) and whether you want larger firms or local lawyers, and I’ll give more targeted recommendations.
